name: Morocco
summary: Morocco taxes residents on worldwide income. Investment income is taxed at flat, final rates: 11.25% on Moroccan dividends paid in 2026 (10% from 2027), 15% on foreign dividends (with credit for foreign tax), 15% on gains on Moroccan-listed shares and 20% on unlisted or foreign shares and on real estate. There is no wealth tax and no inheritance tax; gifts to children bear 1.5% registration duty. Casablanca Finance City is a company regime and offers no personal tax relief to a passive investor.

regimes.name: Moroccan tax resident
regimes.description: Worldwide income tax 0-37% on ordinary income; flat final rates on dividends and gains.
regimes.eligibility: Resident if the permanent home or centre of economic interests is in Morocco, or on presence of more than 183 days in any 365-day period. Non-Moroccans need a residence card (carte de séjour).

capital_gains.summary: Gains on financial instruments are taxed at flat rates: 15% on listed shares and 20% on unlisted shares and bonds (PwC). Gains on foreign securities are 'profits de source étrangère' taxed at 20% (Upsilon, citing the CGI 2026). Real estate gains are taxed at 20%, with a minimum tax of 3% of the sale price; a principal residence occupied for at least six years is exempt.

sources.title: Revenus de capitaux mobiliers au Maroc : dividendes, intérêts, RAS et déclaration

open_questions: Treatment of gains on foreign real estate for a resident (20% foreign-source rate assumed) not confirmed in the CGI text.
Whether foreign-listed shares can use the 15% listed-share rate was not confirmed; Upsilon gives 20% for foreign-source profits.
capital_gains.rate_basis: Flat final rates: listed (Casablanca Stock Exchange) shares 15%; foreign shares 20% (foreign-source profits); unlisted shares 20%; real estate 20% (minimum 3% of price). Foreign real estate assumed to fall under the 20% foreign-source rate.
capital_gains.holding_period_rules: None for securities; principal residence exemption after six years of occupation.
capital_gains.professional_trader: Regular property dealing or securities trading as a business is taxed as professional income at up to 37%.
capital_gains.foreign_assets: Residents are taxed on worldwide gains; foreign tax credit under Art. 77 CGI where tax was paid in a treaty country.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Since the 2026 Finance Law, foreign-source investment income and gains not withheld by a Moroccan intermediary must be declared under Art. 84 bis CGI by 1 April of the following year.

dividends.summary: Moroccan dividends paid to individuals in 2026 bear an 11.25% final withholding tax (12.5% in 2025, 10% from 2027; Art. 247-XXXVII-C CGI). Foreign dividends received by residents are taxed at a flat 15% final rate (Art. 73-II-C CGI), withheld by a Moroccan bank or declared, with credit for foreign tax paid in a treaty country up to the Moroccan tax.

sources.title: Revenus de capitaux mobiliers au Maroc : dividendes, intérêts, RAS et déclaration
Fiscalité internationale des dividendes au Maroc — CGI 2026, conventions et IGOC

open_questions: PwC (reviewed 30 April 2026) still shows the 2025 dividend rate of 12.5%; the 11.25% 2026 rate is from Upsilon citing the CGI and was not checked against the DGI text.
dividends.rate_basis: Domestic 11.25% (2026 payment year). Foreign 15% gross before credit; a 15% US treaty WHT would leave no Moroccan tax.
dividends.withholding_outbound: 11.25% in 2026 (10% from 2027), reduced under treaties (e.g. 10%/15% US, 15% France).
dividends.treaty_network: About 50 DTTs including the US, UK, France, Germany, Spain, Italy, Netherlands, Switzerland, UAE and Qatar.
dividends.holding_company_notes: CIT 20% (35% above MAD 100 million taxable income); participation exemption for dividends from Moroccan companies.

wealth_tax.property_tax_note: Local taxes on property: taxe d'habitation and taxe de services communaux (rates not verified here). Registration duties of 1-6% on property transfers.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance tax: transfers on death are not subject to registration duty. Gifts (hiba) between ascendants and descendants bear a reduced 1.5% registration duty on the market value (CGI art. 133-I-C-4°). Succession follows the Moudawana's fixed shares for Muslim Moroccans; foreigners' successions follow their national law (not verified).

sources.title: Testament, donation, héritage au Maroc 2026 : règles et fiscalité

open_questions: Whether a gift of foreign listed securities by deed triggers the 1.5% registration duty was not verified.
inheritance.gift_tax: 1.5% registration duty on gifts to children (on the property's market value), plus land registry and notary costs; scored as a cost, not a gift tax.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Partition deeds between heirs bear 1.5%; land registry (ANCFCC) and adoul/notary fees apply on Moroccan real estate.
inheritance.foreign_assets: No inheritance tax on any asset; registration duty applies to deeds registered in Morocco.

residency.tax_residency_test: Resident if (in order) the permanent home is in Morocco, the centre of economic interests is in Morocco, or the person stays more than 183 days in any 365-day period (PwC).

routes.name: Carte de séjour (residence card)
routes.requirements: Foreigners staying beyond 90 days apply for a residence card (e.g. on the basis of means of subsistence, property or business); Morocco has no golden-visa programme verified in this session.

corporate.summary: CIT 20% on taxable income below MAD 100 million and 35% above (FY 2026); 40% for banks and insurers; minimum contribution 0.25% of turnover. Dividend WHT 11.25% in 2026.
corporate.special_zones: Casablanca Finance City (CFC) companies and Industrial Acceleration Zones: 20% rate. CFC is a corporate status; its employee salary regime does not help a passive investor.

sources.title: Morocco - Corporate - Taxes on corporate income

us_citizen_notes: US citizens remain fully US-taxed on worldwide income and estates; the app adds the US federal layer. US-Morocco income tax treaty (1977) in force.
open_questions: CGI 2026 text on the DGI site (tax.gov.ma) returned HTTP 403; statutory articles are cited from professional summaries.
